messages:
Jess: Quick flag — when hosted pool returns 429 we fall back to dedicated but latency jumps and responses lose prefix cache. Noticing ~3x per-token latency on a small repro. Anyone else seen this?
Sam: Reproducible here. Looks like we spin up a runtime without KV warmup; fallback route creates a fresh session. :grimacing:
Oliver: Is fallback choosing a different model variant (int8 vs quant)? That would explain perf delta.
Jess: Not a variant change — same model id. Suspect we skip cache warm restore. Pasting current routing snippet: 
Jess: ```yaml
routing:
  prefer: hosted
  fallback: dedicated
  fallback_behavior:
    preserve_kv_cache: false
    preserve_session: false
```
Tara: That's the problem — preserve_kv_cache default=false. RFC we landed in 2023 set that to false to avoid cross-tenant leakage. We discussed snapshot handshake as a safe path but never implemented.
Sam: Confirmed adapter code path doesn't pass any snapshot handle during the fallback flow.
InfraBot: Deploy finished: rollout/hosted-fallbacks v2 -> canary (3 hosts). No impact expected.
Oliver: Short-term mitigation idea: gate preserve_kv_cache behind capability negotiation from the dedicated runtime (accepts_snapshot: true). If capability present, restore; otherwise cold start.
Jess: Agreed. Also need to emit a metric fallback_cache_restored and a tag with tenant id so we can audit correctness and leakage risk.
Tara: Operationally we should default to opt-in for external customers, opt-out for internal. Also add an audit log entry when a snapshot is restored.
Sam: I'll open an issue with a test matrix: baseline latency, fallback cold vs warmed, and a security test for cache isolation.
Jess: Proposed plan: (1) adapter: add handshake to ask dedicated runtime for accepts_snapshot capability; (2) control plane: pass encrypted snapshot handle when capability present; (3) runtime: accept+validate snapshot and restore KV cache; (4) metrics+audit.
InfraBot: Created ticket INF-789: "fallback-kv-snapshot-handshake" — https://redwood/INF-789
Oliver: I'll add the metric and a small dashboard tile for fallback latency vs restored cache.
Tara: I'll draft a short RFC addendum focused on the handshake and the security constraints (KMS flow, TTL on snapshots, tenant-scoped keys).
Sam: Quick Q: do we need a migration path for older dedicated clusters that don't implement the handshake?
Jess: Yes — we treat them as capability=false and fall back to cold start. We'll annotate the rollout notes so customers know.
Sam: Got it. Creating the issue with links to this thread and a minimal repro.
Jess: Thanks all. If nobody objects I'd like a 15-min sync to unblock Sam tomorrow.
Sam: I'll join. :thumbsup:
